workingTitle: Euclid resolves fifteen exceptionally faint stellar systems
publicationStatus: Euclid Collaboration preprint submitted November 11, 2026; intended for the Astronomy & Astrophysics Euclid DR1 special issue and not yet peer reviewed
coreFacts: A resolved-star search across about 1,900 square degrees of Euclid Wide Survey DR1 data identified 15 low-surface-brightness stellar systems that had never previously been resolved into individual stars.
Five are new discoveries: three in the Milky Way halo and two beyond the Local Group; the other ten were previously catalogued as unresolved dwarf-galaxy candidates.
Ursa Minor II is about 20 kiloparsecs away and has an estimated stellar mass near 40 solar masses, making it one of the least luminous known stellar systems.
Eridanus V lies about 165 kiloparsecs away and has an estimated stellar mass near 550 solar masses, in the size-luminosity overlap between globular clusters and ultra-faint dwarf galaxies.
The 12 systems beyond the Local Group lie about 3 to 5.5 megaparsecs away, and ten are candidate members of the M81 group.
The classifications and memberships of several systems remain uncertain; follow-up spectroscopy and deeper imaging are needed.
sourceStatus: Full primary preprint, arXiv metadata, and Euclid Consortium DR1 science spotlight read; critical counts, distances, masses, and caveats checked.
caveats: The paper is an unreviewed preprint intended for an Astronomy & Astrophysics special issue.
Not all 15 objects are new discoveries; ten were known as unresolved sources but are resolved into stars here for the first time.
Several objects have uncertain classifications or group memberships.
